title: Ironwright as a hosted product, one tenant's journey

captions.text: Northwind Mutual is an insurer with old systems. It signs up here, on the hosted stack.
Three real shapes of mess: a fixed width policy file, a billing export, an agency's spreadsheet.
I read each file by rules, not by model. Every guess comes with its reason.
Nobody told me where the joins are. I found them from the values.
No SQL to write. I draft the cleaning and count the rows each decision touches.
I guessed client_key. A person knows policy_nbr is the real key, so they change it.
Bronze, silver and gold run as a background job, with quality gates on the way.
The badge says L1: real files, so no planted answers to check against. I say so.
I propose objects and links, each with its reason. Nothing goes live until a person accepts.
Ask a real question. Rules gather the facts, and every claim cites what it stands on.
The evidence ids are what the agent really gathered. Anything else gets rewritten.
This one is out of reach of the ontology, so I refuse and say why.
Now an action. The policy parks it, and nothing changes until a person decides.
Approved, with that person's identity on the record.
Every step lands in a hash chain. The server recomputes all of it on demand.
Rival Co shares this stack. Signed in there, none of Northwind's work is listed.
Rival asks for Northwind's real upload id. It gets the same 404 as an id that never existed.
Back at Northwind: what it used today, against its plan's limits.
That is the whole journey, on the same stack a customer gets.
